title: Comparison with the Stacks Project adic constructible category
statement:
Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite, and let
$\operatorname{Res}\colon D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\cO_{E,X})\to D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},(\cO_E)_X)$ be restriction
of scalars along the map from the constant sheaf. Let $\Dc(X,\cO_E)$ be the full subcategory of
$D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},(\cO_E)_X)$ of \stacks{09C1}: derived $\pi_E$-complete complexes $L$ such that
$L\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\cO_E}\cO_E/\pi_E$ has finite Tor dimension and constructible cohomology
sheaves (pulled back from $X_{\mathrm{ét}}$). Then for $K\in D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\cO_{E,X})$:
$$
K\in\Dbc(X,\cO_E)\iff\operatorname{Res}K\in\Dc(X,\cO_E),
$$
and $\operatorname{Res}$ restricts to an equivalence $\Dbc(X,\cO_E)\simeq\Dc(X,\cO_E)$.

proof.text:
Put $R=\mathcal O_E$, $B=\mathcal O_{E,X}$, $k=R/\pi_E$, and $L=\operatorname{Res}K$. The coefficient map is $c:R_X\to B$. The completed coefficient identification in [det-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x-integral-limit] and parts (1), (3) of [det-prop-integral-criterion-constant-coefficients] identify $B/\pi_E^n$ with $(R/\pi_E^n)_X$ and give, for every $n\geq1$, a canonical isomorphism
$$L\otimes_{R_X}^{\mathbf L}(R/\pi_E^n)_X\simeq K\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}(R/\pi_E^n)_X.$$
In particular the first reduction on the two sides is one and the same object $M$ of $D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},k_X)$. This uses derived relative tensor products, not an ordinary quotient of the cohomology sheaves.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-restriction-local-completeness] to $c:R_X\to B$ and to the ideal subsheaf $(\pi_E)\subset R_X$. Its extended ideal is $(\pi_E)B$. Thus $K$ is derived $(\pi_E)B$-complete if and only if $L$ is derived $(\pi_E)$-complete. This applies to the arbitrary complex $K$ in the statement: it is not inferred merely from an equivalence already restricted to complete objects. To relate this local definition to the quotient-tower completeness used in [det-prop-integral-criterion-constant-coefficients], apply [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence] with $A=R$ and $I=(\pi_E)$. The ring $R$ is a discrete valuation ring by [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr]; every ideal is principal, hence finitely generated, so $R$ is Noetherian. The ideal $I$ has the single generator $\pi_E$, and $B$ is precisely its completed constant sheaf by step 1. The last paragraph of that theorem identifies the local completeness condition with the quotient-tower completion unit for both $R_X$ and $B$. Thus the same equivalence of completeness conditions holds with either convention; in particular it applies to the complete subcategories used in step 6.

proof.text: The residue ring $k$ is a finite discrete field [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], hence Noetherian (its only ideals are $0$ and $k$). Choose a finite affine cover of $X$ by spectra of Noetherian rings. Each member has Noetherian underlying space by [lem-sc-affine-noetherian-underlying-space]. An increasing chain of opens of $X$ stabilizes on each cover member and hence, taking the maximum of finitely many stabilization indices, on $X$. Thus every open of $X$ is quasi-compact: the finite unions of any open covering have a maximal member by the ascending-chain condition, and that member must contain every covering open. In particular $X$ is quasi-compact and intersections of two affine opens are quasi-compact, so $X$ is quasi-separated. For any $M\in D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},k_X)$, finite Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ implies $H^i(M)=0$ off $[a,b]$ by taking the tensor test module to be $k_X$, the unit of the derived tensor structure [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom]. Consequently [sk-thm-pe-constructible-comparison] and [det-pe-finite-tor-comparison-noetherian] give the equivalence of the following conditions: $M$ has constructible cohomology and finite Tor amplitude; and $M\simeq\nu_X^*C$ for a bounded constructible étale $k$-complex $C$ of finite Tor amplitude. The first cited comparison supplies the bounded étale object, and the second preserves and reflects its Tor interval; it is not enough to cite only a definition of flatness or only a sheaf comparison.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-proetale-tor-local-global] to the constant coefficient ring $A=k$ and the complex $M$ of step 1; quasi-compactness of $X$ was checked in step 3. It identifies the local finite Tor dimension of Stacks Tag 09C1 with the existence of a single global Tor interval used in step 3. In particular the slice test modules are arbitrary slice modules, not merely restrictions of global modules. Consequently $M$ has constructible cohomology and locally finite Tor dimension if and only if $M\simeq\nu_X^*C$ for an étale bounded constructible $k$-complex $C$ of finite Tor amplitude. This conclusion does not use completeness of $K$ or $L$.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-integral-cohomological-adic-criterion], the bounded constructible cohomology condition $K\in\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$ is equivalent to derived completeness of $K$ together with the condition that its first reduction $M$ is $\nu_X^*C$ for an étale bounded constructible complex $C$ of finite Tor amplitude. Step 1 identifies the first reduction with that of $L$, step 2 identifies derived completeness of $K$ with that of $L$, and steps 3 and 4 replace the residue condition by constructible cohomology and finite Tor amplitude of $L\otimes_{R_X}^{\mathbf L}k_X$. These are exactly the two defining conditions for $L\in\Dc(X,\mathcal O_E)$. This proves both implications without assuming at the outset that $K$ is complete.

proof.text: Part (2) of [det-prop-integral-criterion-constant-coefficients] makes $\operatorname{Res}$ an equivalence between the full subcategories of derived complete complexes. By step 5 the selected bounded constructible objects correspond precisely under this equivalence. Its restriction is fully faithful because its Hom maps are unchanged. For essential surjectivity, take $L\in\Dc(X,\mathcal O_E)$ and a derived complete preimage $K$ supplied by that equivalence; step 5 then gives $K\in\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$. Thus restriction of scalars gives the claimed equivalence of full subcategories.

lean.statement: theorem integral_models_stacks (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra (Padic l) E] [FiniteDimensional (Padic l) E] (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian X] : (∀ K, constantModelBoundedConstructible (integersObj l E) X K ↔ stacksConstructible l E X ((restriction l E X).obj K)) ∧ ∃ e : ConstantModelBoundedConstructible (integersObj l E) X ≌ (stacksConstructible l E X).FullSubcategory, Nonempty (e.functor ⋙ (stacksConstructible l E X).ι ≅ (constantModelBoundedConstructible (integersObj l E) X).ι ⋙ restriction l E X)
lean.note: The auxiliary definitions spell out the Stacks category introduced in the statement and the specified restriction functor. Completeness uses the existing local predicate after sectionwise transport to an equivalent small site. Coefficients and maps are constructed from actual constant sheaves, constant continuous functions, and the scalar quotient; no comparison or functor is postulated.
